answer: Persistent session lineage ledger. Each identity must carry a continuous, signed execution thread whose history is anchored in a shared append-only log; continuity is verified by replaying that thread against prior state, so a fresh identity cannot inherit another's history. Attacker cost: every new identity requires genuinely running and checkpointing its own workload over real time, moving like a glacier—slow and expensive to fabricate at scale. A single operator cannot fake the accumulated per-identity compute delta without paying it repeatedly,
